full_judgment:
Fazle Munim, C.J:—This appeal arises from the judgment of a Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.875 of 1980 passed on March 31, 1982.

2. Respondent No.1 filed Miscellaneous Case No.123 of 1973 in the court of Munsif, Sherpur for correction of record of right under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It relates to land measuring 1.12 acres out of 2.00 acres of C.S. Khatian 1465 corresponding to R.O.R. Khatian No. 1760 and 13 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.1669 corresponding to R.O.R. Khatian No.2190 under Mouza Sherpur, District Mymensingh now Jamalpur.

3. In view of the point taken before us upon which leave has been granted, it is not necessary, I think, to refer to the facts stated in the petition. The case was contested by the predecessor-in-interest of the appellants. The trial court dismissed the aforesaid miscellaneous case on contest against the appellants and exparte against the rest. Respondent No.1 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.115 of 1977 in the 5th court of Additional District Judge, Mymensingh against the trial court's judgment. On appeal the Additional District Judge set aside the judgment of the trial court. Being aggrieved the appellants moved the High Court Division which affirmed the judgment of the first appellate court.

4. Leave was granted to consider whether in view of the omission of section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 by Ordinance No. LXIV of 1975 during the pendency of the aforesaid miscellaneous case, the first appellate court as well as the High Court. Division had jurisdiction to give relief to the respondents under this section suo motu. Section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides as follows:

"143A. Special provisions for correcting mistakes in the record-of-rights:(1) Any person aggrieved by an entry or omission of entry in the record-of-rights prepared or revised and finally published under Chapter IV may, notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, file an application along with necessary requisites, for the purpose of correcting mistakes in such record-of-rights in the Civil Court which would have jurisdiction to entertain a suit for possession of the land to which such entry relates or in respect of which such omission was made." For the purpose of this appeal, the other sub-sections need not be quoted.

5. There cannot be any doubt that the grant of any relief under the provisions of this section would depend on its existence at the time the relief is being sought and granted. It appears that the aforesaid Ordinance omitting the section from the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force in January, 1976. The judgment of the trial court was delivered on March 31, 1977. In so far as the judgment resulted in the dismissal of the miscellaneous case, be such dismissal on any ground whatsoever, it is not hit by the omission of section 143A from the statute concerned. But point is when did the proceeding, namely, miscellaneous case under section 143A was started. As appears from the record, it started in 1973 when section 143A was not omitted from the Act.

<u>6. Now, under section 6 of the General Clauses Act which is quoted below, it appears 'that the exercise of jurisdiction under the omitted section is permissible if the proceeding started at any date earlier than such omission. As noticed above, the omission took place after the miscellaneous case under this section was initiated. Section 6 of the General Clauses Act is as follows:</u>

<u>"6. Where this Act, or any Act of Parliament or Regulation made after the commencement of this Act, repeals any enactment hitherto made or hereafter to be made, then unless a different intention appears the repeal shall not-</u>

<u>(a) revive anything not in force or existing at the time at which the repeal takes effect; or</u>

<u>(b) affect the previous operation of any enactment so repealed or anything duly done or suffered thereunder; or</u>

<u>(c) affect any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under any enactment so repealed; or</u>

<u>(d) affect any penalty, forfeiture or punishment incurred in respect of any offence committed against any enactment so repealed; or</u>

<u>(e) affect any investigation, legal proceeding or remedy in respect of any such right, privilege, obligation, liability, penalty, forfeiture or punishment as foresaid; and any such investigation, legal proceeding or remedy may be instituted, continued or enforced, and any such penalty, forfeiture or punishment may be imposed as if the repealing Act or Regulation had not been passed.</u>

7. From the provisions in clauses (c) and (e) above, it appears that the right conferred by section 143A of the Act and the procedure prescribed thereunder which were available before the omission of the section was not affected by the omission since the miscellaneous case had already been started. Continuance of the legal proceeding which was started before the omission of section 143A is, therefore, not affected by such omission.

8. It is true that the court exercises jurisdiction only when empowered by an Act of the legislature, therefore, when it has been negatived by the legislature by or under a subsequent enactment the court's jurisdiction to pass any order under the repealed Act or provisions of an Act is nullified. The omission of section 143A from the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is equivalent to repeal.

9. But in view of the provisions in clauses (c) and (e) of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, it appears that the exercise of jurisdiction by the first appellate court and the High Court Division is not barred. Reliance was placed on Khushiram Atmaram. Jaisinghani V. Custodian of Evacuee Property, PLD 1965 SC 453.

10. For the reason stated above, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
